new_assertions.body: The transitive closure of the four PMEC pair-key equality relations is the finest deterministic quotient factoring all four maps on a declared source domain. This is a finite structural universal property, not scalar qualification.

For each sign D=x+y and A=abs(x-y); D>=A and D-A even are necessary and sufficient before clipping. Clip3(D),clip2(A) admit seven single-sign categories and 49 two-sign pair states. This is owner-count feasibility, not full board or triangle realizability.

The four PMEC maps on the feasible domain have 40,40,39,42 classes and their finest common quotient has 31. The Cartesian control has 144 states, carrier counts 72,72,63,80, and 30 common classes. The counts refer to different domains.

The feasible common quotient distinguishes 16 of 49 states from simultaneous sign reversal. D-only or A-only reversal remains indistinguishable on each operation's 29 in-domain states; intermediate independent reversals need not be feasible. The Cartesian quotient distinguishes no reversal.

Pair quotienting, triangle assembly and GF(2) dependency image formation need not commute. Exactness of the four RS077 triangle carriers does not qualify their common pair quotient. No scalar replay or coefficients were used in RS078.

Domain restriction can increase common-quotient class count by removing impossible connecting states. Independent reversal invariance on a partial domain does not entail simultaneous reversal invariance.
RS077 whole-grid sequencing is requalified by a repaired full replay with byte-identical raw evidence; this does not retroactively change the historical execution or validate new scalar candidates.
